channel.title: RSS Aggregator Feed
channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: Syncing Apple Music across your devices is easier than you think
item.description: One perk of subscribing to Apple Music is having your collection synced across all your devices - and all it takes is a simple toggle. Here's how.

item.title: Just a moonshot? Google energy head claims data centers in space would cost up to 100x more than on Earth
item.description: Google is running AI chips in orbit, but its own data center energy chief says space data centers could, if scaled, cost up to 100x as much as building on Earth.

item.title: 'The next generation won’t replace this one so much as sit on top of it' — Industry analysts say Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo's 'relentless push for higher-end performance will need to be moderated' to avoid $1000 launch consoles
item.description: Industry analysts have suggested console manufacturers will need to temper their ambitions for next-gen to avoid breaching the $1000 console launch mark.

item.title: Samsung One UI 9.5 beta may be coming soon: Here's how to sign up for the program
item.description: Samsung appears to be preparing the One UI 9.5 beta program ahead of an expected 2027 launch. Here's what to do if you want to test Samsung's latest OS.

item.title: How do spam callers get your number in the first place?
item.description: Ever wonder how a total stranger ended up with your phone number? The answer starts earlier than you think, and a few small habits can keep it from spreading.

item.title: What does Apple One Family come with and which subscription is best for you?
item.description: Apple One offers strong value if you're using a lot of Apple services anyway, but make sure you do the math before signing up.

item.title: 10 useful iPad apps that could make your daily life easier
item.description: Your iPad can do a lot with the right apps. Go beyond Apple's defaults and try these useful offerings that all have great free tiers.

item.title: Drones can now be tracked down by mobile networks alone — could this new Ericsson tech spell the end for the current crop of flying UAVs?
item.description: Ericsson is developing mobile network technology that detects and tracks drones, with commercial trials planned for 2027 and wider deployment in 2028.
